llm_commentary: Baseline on c8a.2xlarge: 8.83s wall = ~1.5s node startup + light 4.09s (48.9k calls/s, p50 1.06ms, p99 5.6ms @c64) + heavy 3.19s (626 calls/s, avg 12.7ms, fastest 7.5ms @c8), so the heavy call costs ~0.75µs per cold SLOAD+keccak iteration and both phases carry real weight in the total. The counters point at the I/O path rather than compute: 44% of CPU time is kernel (sys 19.7s vs user 25.3s), thread utilization is only 2.91x on 8 vCPUs, and IPC 1.72 with an 11.2% dTLB miss rate is typical of mmap-heavy MDBX page walks plus loopback HTTP syscalls. The light phase is therefore likely bounded by jsonrpsee/hyper + kernel networking (and the co-located oha client competing for cores), while the heavy phase is bounded by per-SLOAD state-provider/MDBX cursor reads, not the EVM interpreter — which means `--jit` should help little until reads get cheaper. No flamegraph was captured (perf.script missing), so next: get a perf-record profile to confirm the MDBX vs revm vs RPC split, then try THP/hugepages for the dTLB misses and pin oha to separate cores (taskset) so the client stops polluting the server-side numbers.
